title: Assignment of Real Estate Purchase Contract
summary: Transfer a buyer's rights under a purchase contract to a new buyer for an assignment fee, with the disclosures many states now require.
useWhen: A buyer under contract (the assignor) transfers the contract to another buyer (the assignee) who will close with the seller.
watchOuts: Many states now regulate wholesaling, including Illinois, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Oregon, Texas, Virginia, Connecticut, Maryland, Tennessee, Wisconsin, Iowa and others. Rules include licensing after a number of deals, written disclosure to the seller and buyer that you hold only an equitable interest, seller cancellation rights and registration. Check the state notes and verify locally before marketing or assigning.
Marketing the property itself, rather than the contract, before you own it can be unlicensed brokerage in many states.
Check that the purchase contract allows assignment. Many contracts and all FHA/VA-related and REO contracts prohibit it or require seller consent.
Assignment fees are often visible to the seller on the closing statement. Some states now require the fee, or its existence, to be disclosed.
The assignor usually remains liable under the original contract unless the seller releases the assignor (a novation).

variables.label: State where the property is located
variables.help: Two-letter code. Massless shows the notes for this state from the state reference (states.json): official forms, required disclosures, closing practice, notarization and recording, executory-contract and wholesaling rules.

variables.label: Assignor name
variables.help: Buyer named in the purchase contract.

variables.label: Purchase contract date
variables.help: Effective date of the original contract.

variables.label: Contract purchase price
variables.help: Price the assignee will pay the seller at closing.

variables.label: Assignment fee
variables.help: Amount the assignee pays the assignor.

variables.label: Assignee's deposit toward the fee
variables.help: Paid at signing to the closing agent.

variables.label: Is the assignee's deposit refundable?
variables.default: refundable only if the seller fails to close
options: refundable only if the seller fails to close
refundable for any reason until the inspection deadline

variables.label: Reimburse assignor's earnest money at closing?
variables.help: Assignee reimburses the earnest money the assignor deposited, or replaces it.

variables.label: Assignor's earnest money amount
variables.help: Amount deposited under the purchase contract.

variables.label: Closing agent
variables.help: Title company or attorney closing the sale.

variables.label: Seller consent
variables.default: the purchase contract allows assignment without consent
options: the purchase contract allows assignment without consent
seller consent will be obtained before closing

variables.label: Seller received a wholesaler or equitable-interest disclosure?
variables.default: yes, a written disclosure was given before the contract
options: yes, a written disclosure was given before the contract
not required in this state (verify locally)
variables.help: Several states require written disclosure to the seller and to buyers.

sections.title: 2. Contract assigned
sections.body: Assignor is the buyer under a purchase contract with {{seller_name}} ("Seller") dated {{contract_date}} for the property at {{property_address}} in {{state}} (the "Purchase Contract"), at a price of {{contract_price}}. A copy of the Purchase Contract and its amendments has been given to Assignee. Assignee initials to confirm receipt: [[initial:assignee]]

sections.title: 3. Assignment
sections.body: Effective on {{assignment_date}}, Assignor assigns to Assignee all of Assignor's rights under the Purchase Contract, and Assignee accepts the assignment and assumes all of the buyer's obligations under it from that date, including closing on or before {{closing_date}} and paying the purchase price.

sections.title: 4. Assignment fee
sections.body: Assignee will pay Assignor an assignment fee of {{assignment_fee}}, payable through {{closing_agent}} at closing. Assignee deposits {{fee_deposit}} toward the fee with the closing agent on signing. This deposit is {{deposit_refundable}}. If the sale does not close because Seller defaults, or because of a contingency in the Purchase Contract that Assignee properly exercises, the deposit is returned to Assignee, unless it is non-refundable.

sections.title: 5. Earnest money
sections.body: At closing, Assignee will reimburse Assignor for the {{assignor_earnest}} earnest money that Assignor deposited under the Purchase Contract, or Assignee will deposit replacement earnest money so Assignor's deposit is returned.

sections.title: 6. Seller consent
sections.body: Status: {{consent_status}}. If consent is required and not obtained before closing, either party may cancel this assignment and Assignee's deposit is returned.

sections.title: 7. Nature of assignor's interest
sections.body: Assignee understands that Assignor (a) does not own the property, (b) holds only an equitable interest as the buyer under the Purchase Contract, (c) is not acting as Assignee's real estate agent or broker, and (d) is profiting from this assignment through the assignment fee. Assignor may not be able to deliver title. Title will come from Seller at closing. Assignee: [[initial:assignee]]

sections.title: 8. Disclosure to seller
sections.body: Assignor states that: {{disclosure_given}}. Assignor is responsible for complying with any wholesaling, licensing, disclosure or registration law of {{state}} that applies to Assignor.

sections.title: 9. Assignor's promises
sections.body: Assignor promises that (a) the Purchase Contract is in effect and has not been amended except as disclosed, (b) Assignor has not previously assigned it, (c) Assignor has not received notice of any default, and (d) Assignor will not amend or terminate the Purchase Contract without Assignee's consent.

sections.title: 10. Assignee's independent evaluation
sections.body: Assignee has relied on its own inspection, valuation and due diligence, not on statements by Assignor. Assignor makes no promise about the property's value, condition, rents, repair costs or after-repair value.

sections.title: 11. Liability
sections.body: Assignee will indemnify Assignor against claims arising from Assignee's failure to perform the buyer's obligations under the Purchase Contract after the assignment. Assignor remains liable to Seller unless Seller releases Assignor in writing.

sections.title: 12. State-specific requirements
sections.body: The property is in {{state}}. The parties will comply with that state's requirements for this transaction, including required seller disclosures and forms, licensing rules, closing and recording requirements, and any mandatory statutory notices. Massless shows a summary of known requirements for {{state}} with this template. That summary is a starting point, may be incomplete or out of date, and is not part of this agreement. Any addendum or disclosure form the state requires will be attached and signed by the parties.

sections.title: 13. General
sections.body: This assignment is governed by the law of {{state}}. It is the entire agreement about the assignment. It may be signed electronically and in counterparts. The closing agent may rely on it to disburse the assignment fee.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Assignor** — {{assignor_name}}

[[sig:assignor]]

Printed name: [[name:assignor]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:assignor:Title]]
Date: [[date:assignor]]

**Assignee** — {{assignee_name}}

[[sig:assignee]]

Printed name: [[name:assignee]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:assignee:Title]]
Date: [[date:assignee]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything.
